standard_prerequisites.name: The statement that every irreducible closed subset of a Noetherian space is a finite union of its irreducible components
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 1505-1508)
standard_prerequisites.use: Closes the minimal-counterexample argument for the finiteness of the components.

standard_prerequisites.name: The statement that an irredundant finite union of closed subsets has exactly those subsets as its irreducible components
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked near the end of the counted proof (source lines 1510-1512)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the finite union into the decomposition into irreducible components.

core_obligations: (1): a descending chain of closed subsets of a subspace comes from a descending chain of closed subsets of the space, whose stabilization forces the original chain to stabilize (proof lines 1479-1489)

(2): if the closed subsets not having finitely many irreducible components were nonempty, the descending chain condition would produce a minimal one; being reducible it splits into two strictly smaller closed subsets, each a finite union of its irreducible components, so the same holds for the union, which after removing redundancies is the decomposition into components, a contradiction (proof lines 1490-1513)
(3): the generic point of an irreducible component is contained in some open subset, and those opens are as asserted (proof lines 1514-1517)
proof_roadmap: (1)：把 T 的递降闭集列写成 T ∩ Z_i，则 Z_1 ⊃ Z_1 ∩ Z_2 ⊃ … 稳定 ⇒ 原列稳定。
(2)：设「不可约分支不是有限多个」的闭集族非空，由降链条件取极小元 Z；Z 可约 ⇒ Z = Z' ∪ Z'' 严格更小 ⇒ 各自是有限个不可约分支之并 ⇒ Z 也是；去掉冗余后用 pick-irreducible-components 得 Z 的分支分解，矛盾。
(3)：不可约分支的泛点落在某个开集中，取这些开集即得。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement collects three properties of a Noetherian topological space: every subspace is Noetherian, there are finitely many irreducible components, and each component contains a nonempty open subset (author lemma at source lines 1469-1477, label lemma-Noetherian). The proof (source lines 1479-1518) transfers the descending chain condition to subspaces, runs a minimal-counterexample argument for finiteness of the components using the reducibility of a minimal bad closed subset and closes it with the irredundant-union statement, and reads off the third assertion from the generic points (proof lines 1479-1517). The minimal-counterexample argument is the substance. H3.
